prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
Summary of key proposals (ideology and attributions removed)

Economy and jobs
- Responsible public finances; stability via independent forecasting; Bank of England independence.
- Industrial strategy focused on green infrastructure, digital and bioscience; expand British Business Bank.
- Repair trade ties with Europe; reduce barriers to goods, services, research and skills.
- Cut energy bills through large-scale home insulation and heat pumps; National Food Strategy to ease food prices; careful mortgage and inflation management.
- Skills: replace apprenticeship levy with flexible skills levy; £5,000 Lifelong Skills Grants (aim to rise to £10,000); National Colleges for key sectors.
- Modernise work rights: new “dependent contractor” status; higher minimum wage for zero‑hours shifts at normal demand; right to request fixed hours; fair Statutory Sick Pay from day one and at least the minimum wage.
- Parental leave/pay as day‑one rights; higher maternity, shared parental and paternity pay.
- Tax changes: restore bank surcharges/levies in real terms; higher Digital Services Tax; fairer capital gains; 4% tax on FTSE‑100 buybacks; one‑off windfall tax on oil and gas profits.

Climate, energy and environment
- Net zero by 2045; 90% of electricity from renewables by 2030; rooftop solar expansion.
- Ten‑year emergency home energy upgrade; zero‑carbon standards for new buildings; social tariff for vulnerable energy users; decouple electricity prices from gas.
- Maintain bans on fracking and new coal; expand storage (hydrogen, batteries, pumped).
- Community energy rights and local grids; more interconnectors with neighbours.
- End sewage discharges: tougher regulator, public‑benefit water companies, real‑time discharge data, binding targets; Clean Air Act; 60m trees/year; stronger environment agencies.
- Deposit return scheme; phase out non‑recyclable single‑use plastics; restore peatlands and blue carbon habitats.

Health and social care
- Right to a GP within seven days (24 hours if urgent); recruit 8,000 GPs; expand pharmacy roles and 24/7 booking.
- Guarantee urgent/emergency NHS dentistry; supervised toothbrushing in early years.
- Mental health hubs for young people; regular mental health check‑ups; specialist in every school; end out‑of‑area placements.
- Cancer: treatment start within 62 days; more radiotherapy machines; more cancer nurses.
- Invest in public health; tackle ambulance delays; modernise NHS estate and IT; faster access to medicines via mutual recognition; health‑led drug policy with regulated cannabis market.
- Social care: free personal care; workforce plan, Royal College of Care Workers, £2/hr Carer’s Minimum Wage; paid carer’s leave and guaranteed respite; National Care Agency and consistent standards.

Education and families
- Per‑pupil funding rises; repair unsafe buildings; tutoring guarantee for disadvantaged pupils.
- Early years: extra free hours for disadvantaged children; higher Early Years Pupil Premium; workforce development and childminding reform.
- Teacher workforce strategy; independent pay review; curriculum and qualifications reform; stronger SEND funding and a new national body.
- Extend free school meals to all children in poverty.
- Enhance parental leave/pay; “Toddler Top‑Up” to Child Benefit; Erasmus+ return; reinstate maintenance grants; Lifelong Skills Grants.

Housing and local government
- Build 380,000 homes/year, including 150,000 social; new garden cities; brownfield incentives; “use‑it‑or‑lose‑it” permissions; rent‑to‑own for social homes.
- End no‑fault evictions; default three‑year tenancies; national landlord register; abolish leasehold and cap ground rents; remove dangerous cladding at no cost to leaseholders.
- End rough sleeping with emergency accommodation duty and funding.
- More local powers and multi‑year funding; control over second homes/short‑lets; universal gigabit broadband.

Crime and justice
- Restore community policing; guarantee police attendance at all burglaries; Online Crime Agency; reduce court backlogs; expand restorative justice and rehabilitation.
- Replace Police and Crime Commissioners with local Police Boards; independent pay review; targets for workforce diversity; specialist domestic‑abuse support; youth diversion nationwide; stronger fraud protections.

Transport
- Accelerate EV charging rollout; restore 2030 zero‑emission sales date; reinstate plug‑in car grant; cut VAT on public charging.
- Freeze rail fares; simplify ticketing; new Railway Agency; electrification plan; Northern Powerhouse Rail; stronger bus franchising and £2 fare cap; national active travel strategy; more funds for local road repairs.

Immigration and asylum
- Shift from blanket enforcement to tackling smuggling/trafficking; streamline, fair work and student visas across departments.
- Repeal offshore asylum plan and recent restrictive asylum law; safe and legal routes; three‑month decision standard; permit work after three months.
- Flexible work‑visa thresholds; fairer family visa rules; expand Youth Mobility; resolve EU citizens’ status and proof; independent Windrush compensation.

Rights, democracy, defence and international
- Uphold Human Rights Act and ECHR; ban conversion practices; roll back recent anti‑protest and live facial recognition powers; stronger disability rights.
- Proportional representation (STV); votes at 16; cap political donations; codify Ministerial Code; reform second chamber; devolved federal constitution; transparency on lobbying and ministerial messaging.
- Increase defence spending towards 2.5% of GDP; reverse Army cuts; improve procurement and service family support; maintain nuclear deterrent while pursuing multilateral disarmament; deepen European security cooperation.
- Rebuild relations with Europe via phased roadmap towards closer market access; support Ukraine including via seized assets; restore aid to 0.7% GNI; back a ceasefire and two‑state framework in the Middle East; robust human‑rights sanctions and BBC World Service funding.
